page.title: 3D Printer with Laser Engraver: H2D vs Artisan Engraving Speed and Price (2026)
page.h1: 3D printer with laser engraver: which combo engraves fastest for the money
page.desc: Bambu Lab H2D and Snapmaker Artisan laser combos compared on rated engraving speed, 100 × 100 mm fill time, laser bed, one-pass cut and today's prices.
page.answer: Short answer. Get the Bambu Lab H2D Laser Full Combo, a 3D printer with a 10 W laser engraver module: it engraves at 400 mm/s, twice the Snapmaker Artisan's 200 mm/s, so a 100 × 100 mm fill at rated speed takes about 4.2 min vs 8.3. Choose the Artisan for CNC and a 400 × 400 mm laser bed.

page.after:
What the differences mean

  • Fill time. A fill engrave is drawn line by line. A 100 × 100 mm patch at 0.1 mm spacing is 1,000 lines × 100 mm = 100,000 mm of travel. H2D 10 W: 100,000 ÷ 400 mm/s = 250 s ≈ 4.2 min. Artisan: 100,000 ÷ 200 mm/s = 500 s ≈ 8.3 min. H2D 40 W: 100,000 ÷ 1,000 mm/s = 100 s ≈ 1.7 min. These are best cases at the maximum rated speed. Real jobs add acceleration, overscan and travel.
  • Laser bed. Artisan: 40 × 40 cm = 1,600 cm². H2D 10 W: 31 × 27 cm = 837 cm². 1,600 ÷ 837 = 1.9× the area on the Artisan.
  • Price gap at 10 W. $1,949 − $1,799 = $150. The extra $150 buys the H2D's 2× rated engraving speed. Saving it gets you the Artisan's 1.9× bed and a 200 W CNC module.
  • Step up to 40 W. H2D: $2,399 − $1,949 = $450 for 2.5× the rated speed (1,000 ÷ 400) and a 15 mm cut rating instead of 5 mm. Artisan: $2,199 − $1,799 = $400 for the same 5 → 15 mm cut rating at the same 200 mm/s. Adding the $429 40 W module to a base Artisan costs $1,799 + $429 = $2,228, which is $29 more than the Premium.
UseFitsWhy
Mostly 3D printing, plus engraved tags, logos and giftsBambu Lab H2D Laser Full Combo 10 WTwice the Artisan's rated engraving speed for $150 more
Cutting thick wood and fast production engravingBambu Lab H2D Laser Full Combo 40 W1,000 mm/s and a 15 mm one-pass rating
Large sheets, CNC carving, lowest priceSnapmaker Artisan1,600 cm² laser bed and 200 W CNC for $1,799
CNC plus thick laser cutsSnapmaker Artisan Premium40 W with air assist and CNC for $2,199

Engraving speed: rated figures and tested settings

Laser power sets how much material each pass can burn at a given speed. Maximum engraving speed sets how long a fill takes. For tags, coasters and photos, which are mostly fill work, the speed rating decides job time more than the wattage does. Bambu Lab rates the H2D's 10 W module at 400 mm/s and its 40 W module at 1,000 mm/s, according to Dynamism's listings of both combos. Snapmaker's Artisan spec sheet gives a single 200 mm/s maximum for both its 10 W and 40 W modules. Snapmaker's page for the standalone 10 W module lists 6,000 mm/min (100 mm/s) alongside Snapmaker 2.0 work areas. The Artisan figures above use the Artisan's own sheet.

Tested settings run below the rated maximums. Alex Tyrer-Jones at 3D Printing Industry got the best results from the Artisan Premium's 40 W laser on 5.2 mm basswood by engraving at 6,000 mm/min (100 mm/s) at 10% power and cutting at 1,300 mm/min at 90% power. At that engraving speed, the 100 × 100 mm fill takes 100,000 ÷ 100 = 1,000 s ≈ 16.7 min. Phillip Keane at 3DPrinting.com cut through 8 mm wood in a single pass with the same 40 W module, about half of the 15 mm rating.

Both machines close the laser in. Dynamism's listing gives the H2D laser module as Class 4 and the complete machine as Class 1 when its protections are working. Snapmaker includes the enclosure with both Artisan models. Snapmaker rates the enclosure's stock exhaust fan at 36 CFM, which it calls sufficient for the 10 W module. For the 20 W and 40 W modules it suggests its 95 CFM Boosted Exhaust Fan ($17.99).

Not recommended

Snapmaker 2.0 A250T / A350T ($799 / $1,049 at Direct 3D Printers). The stock laser is 1,600 mW and Snapmaker lists it as Class 4. The open frame needs Snapmaker's separately sold $269 enclosure to reach Class 1. That brings the A350T to $1,049 + $269 = $1,318 for a 1.6 W laser. The Artisan costs $1,799 with a 10 W laser, an enclosure and CNC included. 3D Printing Industry scored the Snapmaker 2.0 63/100 and the Artisan 83/100.
